answer: Terrace-vine sap proof — one $38 sap-flow sensor per identity. One vine row on a real terraced hillside is the identity's body: its sensor reports the vine's daily sap flow, checked against the vineyard's public irrigation log and the row's jade-green canopy in the drone survey. A reading from any other terrace misses the log by litres; a claimed row with no living vine shows bare soil and fails at once. One row carries one identity: a second claim repeats the same flow, and both are struck. Sensors are cheap, rows are not: a terrace takes a season to grow, and a fake has no season to spend.
